questions.question: After you start the engine, how quickly should the oil pressure reach normal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Engine oil pressure should reach normal within seconds after you start the engine. Do not drive if oil pressure is too low.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: You can usually drive faster than a train.
Do not rely only on warning signals.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Only check the track closest to your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on warning signals.
questions.explanation: Never rely only on warning signals to tell you a train is coming. Never try to race a train across the tracks. If there are multiple tracks, check all of them in both directions before crossing.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver has their high beams on, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your high beams to tell them to turn theirs off.
Look toward the right edge of your lane until they pass.
Pull to the side of the road until they pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane until they pass.
questions.explanation: Look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: When should you check your mirror adjustment?

options.text: Only if you plan to use the mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every trip.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before every trip. Adjust them as needed.

questions.question: What is the best approach to speed when driving?

options.text: Always drive at the posted speed limit.
Always drive below the posted speed limit.
Change your speed based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes many serious crashes. Always change your speed to match road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How many drinks does it take for a 200-pound person to reach 0.02 percent blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your driving long before you reach the legal limit. A 200-pound person reaches 0.02 percent BAC after just one drink.

questions.question: When inspecting air and electrical lines, which is NOT correct?

options.text: Air hoses are making a hissing noise.
Air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
Air lines are not dragging on tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: Listen for leaks in air lines during inspection. Air hoses and electrical lines should not be cut, worn, or chafed. They should not be tangled, pinched, or dragging on tractor parts.

questions.question: If a vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Let the vehicle pass.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create more space in front of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden braking, which could cause a rear-end collision, and makes it easier for the tailgater to pass. Speeding up makes things more dangerous.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When vehicles are too close together.

questions.correctAnswerText: When drivers turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn or change lanes too quickly.

questions.question: Is rough acceleration a good practice?

options.text: No, it can damage the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can cause mechanical damage to your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you avoid driving aggressively?

options.text: Plan trips without extra time for traffic.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Do not make gestures at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make gestures at other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan trips with extra time for traffic. Do not tailgate. Do not drive slowly in the left lane or gesture at other drivers, as this upsets them.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, how often must you check that it is secure?

options.text: Every 150 miles or every three hours of driving.
Only after driving up a hill.
Only after making a hard stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or every three hours of driving.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safe during the entire trip.

questions.question: During the driving skills test, if you need to stop before turning, what should you do?

options.text: Stop after the stop line for a better view.
Keep your front wheels pointed straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your front wheels pointed straight.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind the stop line or stop sign. Keep your front wheels straight and do not let your vehicle roll. Stop where you can still see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when driving?

options.text: Hide your driving intentions from others.
Use turn signals only if other vehicles are nearby.
Do not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers what you plan to do. Signal before turning or changing lanes, even if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth required for front tires?
questions.correctAnswerText: 4/32 inch.
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires must have at least 2/32 inch of tread depth.

questions.question: What should bus emergency exit signs be like?

options.text: They can be hidden by cargo.
They do not need to be displayed.
They should be easy to see and identify.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be easy to see and identify.
questions.explanation: Emergency exit signs on a bus must always be clearly visible. The emergency door light must work properly.

questions.question: During the steering box inspection, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the steering box is securely mounted.
Check that the steering box has no leaks.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Check that the steering box is securely mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Make sure there are no power steering fluid leaks and no damaged hoses.

questions.question: What condition should belts in the engine be in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tight.
questions.explanation: Check that engine belts are tight and not excessively worn. The right amount of tightness varies by vehicle, so learn what is correct for yours.

questions.question: Which of these is required emergency equipment?

options.text: A supply of spare electrical fuses.

questions.correctAnswerText: A supply of spare electrical fuses.
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles like reflective triangles.

questions.question: If your vehicle is too long during inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Cut down the length of the load.
Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are fastened securely.
questions.explanation: If your load is oversize, confirm that all required signs, flags, lights, and reflectors are properly mounted. Make sure you have all required permits.
